news.name: Remembering George W. Bush's Secret 2003 Thanksgiving Visit to Iraq Troops
news.summary: Only a few knew about the trip as Bush landed at Baghdad International Airport around 5:30 p.m. on November 27, stepping out in an Army track jacket to cheers after L. Recent posts highlight the gesture's warmth alongside sharp divides, with some calling it a class act and others tying it to the war's heavy toll.

news.hook: On Thanksgiving Eve, a brilliant green fireball raced across southern Michigan skies, turning heads and cameras just before 8 p.m. Crowds at Indiana's Night of Lights even caught it mid-drone show.
news.name: Green Fireball Meteor Lights Up Midwest Skies on Thanksgiving Eve
news.summary: The meteor, a tau Taurid estimated at over 120 pounds and 14 inches wide, appeared 67 miles above Imlay City, Michigan, hurtling at 61,000 mph before breaking apart 32 miles over Bath. Over 1,300 witnesses from the Midwest, Northeast, and Ontario reported the full-Moon-bright streak, captured on security cams, dashcams, and even the GOES-19 satellite. No ground impacts occurred, as it burned up high in the atmosphere, leaving drivers on I-75 and locals in Ohio and Michigan sharing stunned accounts of the green glow and smoke trail.

news.hook: Imagine pigeons with brain implants and tiny cameras, soaring on command for stunning aerial shots. A Moscow company just turned this sci-fi idea into a real service.
news.name: Russian Firm Launches Pigeons as Remote-Controlled Biodrones
news.summary: Neiry, based in Moscow, fits pigeons with biocompatible brain electrodes, solar-powered backpacks, GPS, and cameras to create PJN-1 biodrones for photography and monitoring power lines or pipelines. Operators control them via electrical signals or flight plans, with tests logging over 100 flights, one lasting more than 10 hours over 100 kilometers. Now in beta commercial service in Russia at 300,000 rubles per square kilometer, the firm claims advantages in endurance over regular drones, while AI blurs faces for privacy and an ethical protocol was approved—though many online voices decry it as animal cruelty.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni shared her deepest sorrow with the victims' families.

news.name: Declassified FBI Files Reveal More CIA Waterboarding Than Admitted
news.summary: Newly released FBI records, obtained via a New York Times FOIA lawsuit linked to the John Durham investigation, indicate the CIA waterboarded more detainees than the three—Abu Zubaydah, Khalid Shaikh Mohammed, and Abd al-Rahim al-Nashiri—it officially acknowledged after 9/11. The key detail comes from the translator who briefly witnessed a session with a detainee called “Bahir” or “Bashir” at the Salt Pit near Kabul, a site not previously associated with the technique. These findings, years after the 2014 Senate report on CIA interrogations, have prompted online reactions from outrage over transparency to calls for accountability.

news.hook: Samantha Power warned of a mounting global death toll from U.S. aid cuts on cable news, but newly released USAID files show her agency's close ties to Big Tech on content moderation.
news.name: Samantha Power Faces Backlash Over Aid Cuts Criticism and USAID Censorship Revelations
news.summary: During her 2021-2025 tenure as USAID head, Power coordinated with YouTube and Meta executives on meetings, partnership drafts, disinformation primers, and content tracking requests, according to documents posted on the USAID website. Power dismisses the files as a 'baffling hodge-podge' meant to deflect from the cuts' human costs, while supporters of the overhaul argue USAID veered into propaganda and needed accountability.
